CHAPTER VI
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional

Article 28
(1) Regional Governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection of children and women victims of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 21
(1) Assistance is carried out by persons and/or institutions that cooperate with PPT.
(2) The assistance mechanism as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Konawe Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Konawe.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Konawe Regency.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes a person who is legally recognized as a Woman.
8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
15. Victim is a child and woman who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return child and woman victims of violence to family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles normally again both in the family and in society.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, or substitute family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization that provides assistance.
25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 24
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 9
Exploitation as referred to in Article 4 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

2.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text DOES state an institutional coordination mechanism. Pasal 23(3) explicitly says the regional government cooperates with multiple external entities across jurisdictions: "pemerintah daerah bekerjasama dengan instansi pemerintah, pemerintah provinsi, pemerintah kabupaten/kota lain" (cooperates with government agencies, the provincial government, and other regency/city governments). This is a clear cross-jurisdiction coordination/cooperation statement. The retrieved English candidates included this same content in [4.1-30] but for indicator 2.1 the retrieved set did not include Pasal 23(3); however, it DID include Pasal 13(1)(f) in [2.1-15] stating the government will pursue creation of "cooperation and coordination" in victim recovery efforts. While less specific than Pasal 23(3), it still establishes a coordination commitment/mechanism at least generally. The judge’s rationale was overly strict in requiring explicit cross-jurisdiction detail within the shown sentences and ignored that the regulation itself mandates cooperation/coordination (Pasal 13(1)(f)), so the No verdict reflects judge reasoning failure given the available evidence of coordination.

Article 16
(1) In order to provide services and protection to children and women from violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT as an integrated service center for children and women victims of violence.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of elements from the Health Office, Youth Education and Sports Office, Social Office, Cooperatives Industry and Trade Office, Population and Civil Registry Office, Women's Empowerment and Family Planning Agency, Community Empowerment Agency, Civil Service Police Unit, Regional General Hospital, Police Resort, Non-Governmental Organizations, and Universities.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be established by Regent's decree.
(4) The provision of services to victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner by PPT.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (4) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.
(6) PPT provides services and temporary protection in the form of safe houses.
(7) In the event that PPT does not yet have a safe house, then victims of violence shall be referred to PPT that has a safe house.
(8) PPT consists of several counseling fields.
(9) The counseling fields as referred to in paragraph (8) shall at minimum consist of:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychology field.
(10) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure of PPT shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 24
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 17
Forms of prevention of violence against children and women carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. Socialization activities of laws and regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of children and women; and
b. Training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing violence against children and women.

4.1.rationale: The original Indonesian policy clearly includes information/education as a primary prevention measure. Pasal 17 states: "Bentuk pencegahan ... dapat dilaksanakan melalui: a. Kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan kepada masyarakat yang berkaitan dengan perlindungan hak-hak anak dan perempuan". This is explicit community outreach/socialization (education/information) related to protecting women’s and children’s rights, which functions as prevention of violence. The retrieved candidate [4.1-21] accurately reflects this, and the judge’s Yes rationale matches the text. Therefore the discrepancy is best explained by the golden label being incorrect (it should be Yes, not No).
